name: libvldmail
listed_description: Your friendly email validation library. No external dependencies (not even regexps).
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README.md (MIT-0, 69 stars, upstream moved to Fossil with nightly Git mirrors) and the CHANGES file were read and grepped for fast, speed, bench, perf, slow and regex: the only regex mention is the design choice 'no regex, no ICU, no other overhead', stated as a feature with no timing. The repo root holds test.c, autotest-cases and the man page, with no benchmark source. Web search for libvldmail benchmark or speed found only unrelated validators (a dev.to regex-free validator with its own 13.7 percent figure, htmlmail) and no result that includes libvldmail.

name: libxmi
listed_description: Function library for rasterizing 2D vector graphics
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. gnu.org, ftp.gwdg.de and t2linux.com were EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the project page, manual and ChangeLog could not be read; no GitHub mirror was found. Web search snippets from distro package pages (SlackBuilds, Gentoo, OpenPorts, Source Mage, GnuWin32, GNU directory) describe it only as a C/C++ library that draws 2-D primitives (wide polylines, circular and elliptical arcs, polygons) into a user-supplied pixel matrix, with no speed claim and no benchmark against Cairo, Skia, AGG or any other rasterizer.

name: lightmapper
listed_description: Single-file library for lightmap baking, using an existing OpenGL renderer. Public domain
reason: Only self-comparison numbers, no external baseline. README.md (1.5k stars) says its 'selective hierarchical interpolation' option gives about a 3.3x speedup on the example scene and up to about 10x on larger lightmaps, but the comparison is the library with the option on versus the same library rendering every texel (the README does not give the exact setting of the reference run), with no hardware, compiler or timing table, and no other lightmapper (Blender Cycles, Unity or Unreal lightmappers, xatlas-based bakers) is timed. No benchmark repo or third-party shootout including it was found. The licence is not tagged on the repo page (README says public domain).

name: linalg.h
listed_description: Single header, public domain, short vector math library for C++.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README.md (968 stars, Unlicense) and linalg.h were grepped for bench, fast, speed, perform, simd and optimi: the README positions it as a lightweight alternative to GLM, Boost.QVM and Eigen on design grounds (consistency, readable syntax) and carries no timing; the four open issues are API requests. Third-party benchmark repos found by search (RasterDuck/vectormathbench, mfoo/Math-Library-Test, heilokchow/math_lib_benchmark, 29thnight/Mathematics) were checked for 'linalg' and 'linmath' and do not include it (vectormathbench covers GLM, DirectXMath, SimpleMath, Sony Vectormath, move::vectormath and Realtime Math).

name: linmath.h
listed_description: A lean linear math library, aimed at graphics programming.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README.md (1.1k stars, WTFPL, 701 bytes) only lists supported types (vec3, vec4, mat4x4, quaternions) and GLSL-compatible layout, with no speed text; the 14 open issues concern quaternion correctness, warnings, documentation and double support, none quote timings. The cglm README (the usual C comparison point) has no mention of linmath, and the benchmark repos checked (vectormathbench, Math-Library-Test, math_lib_benchmark) do not include linmath.h.

name: list.h
listed_description: Implementations for singly linked and doubly linked list functions.
reason: No performance claim or number at all. README.md (52 stars, GPL-3.0, last commit 2024-02-24) documents the SL_ and DL_ macros only; src/list.h has no mention of fast, speed, bench or perf; tests/ holds 17 functional tests (test0.c to test16.c with .res files and run_tests.sh), no timing code. Web search for a comparison with utlist or sys/queue found nothing that mentions it.
